newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds continue to underperform.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds continue to underperform.

text.p: Australian bonds continued Tuesday's underperformance against other dollar bloc bonds, although yield spreads were above their initial highs after the Japanese quarterly Tankan report came in weak.

Analysts said as the Japanese economy remained in the doldrums, this allayed concerns of a policy tightening there, which would have otherwise eroded Australia's yield advantage and the lure of yield seeking Japanese investors.

However, local technicals have turned mildly bearish, which saw futures sell off heavily again in early trading and the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread was forced above 100 basis points for the second day in a row.
U.S. Treasuries, meanwhile, also perked up on the Tankan report in Tokyo trading after reversing an initial firm trend in New York trading on Tuesday.
The U.S. market faces a feast of indicators during a shortened session later today ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday.
Offshore buying saw Canadian bonds also outperform the U.S., while New Zealand bonds cemented their 10-year yield to discount to Australia after breaking parity on Tuesday.
